alerts.title: Rising creatinine on TDF warrants monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients initiating TDF, and list chronic kidney disease and Fanconi syndrome as TDF toxicities. Patient's creatinine rose from 0.8 to 1.1 mg/dL and eGFR declined to 78 mL/min/1.73m² after 10 weeks on TDF. This upward creatinine trend warrants attention even though the absolute value remains near-normal. DTG and pregnancy also contribute. Evidence for drug attribution: TDF is nephrotoxic and the rise is temporally associated with initiation. Evidence against: pregnancy itself can affect renal parameters, and eGFR of 78 may reflect normal physiologic adaptation. Urinalysis is normal with no protein or glucose, arguing against significant tubular damage.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat serum creatinine and eGFR at next visit. If creatinine continues rising or eGFR declines further, evaluate for TDF toxicity and consider renal-safe alternatives.

alerts.title: Viral load measured early; repeat at 6 months
alerts.message: Guidelines state the first viral load for adults should be done 6 months after ART initiation, with a repeat VL >1000 copies/mL suggesting treatment failure. This patient's VL was checked at 10 weeks (89 copies/mL), which is earlier than the recommended 6-month schedule. While the result shows good early response, a VL at 6 months per protocol is still needed to confirm sustained suppression. The current VL of 89 copies/mL is above the 200 copies/mL suppression threshold mentioned in guidelines, indicating low-level viremia that should be monitored.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule repeat viral load at 6 months post-ART initiation per guideline schedule to confirm sustained suppression.

alerts.title: No glucose screening documented on DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines require screening for hyperglycaemia risk factors when initiating DTG, with random blood glucose testing if 2 or more risk factors are present. This patient is on DTG and pregnant, but no blood glucose screening or risk factor assessment is documented. Pregnancy itself impairs glucose tolerance, making DTG-associated hyperglycaemia an additional concern. No RBS result appears in today's labs.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess hyperglycaemia risk factors and perform random blood glucose if indicated, given DTG use and pregnancy.

alerts.title: HBV screening status not documented
alerts.message: Guidelines state all PLHIV initiating ART should be routinely screened for HBV using HBsAg. No HBsAg result is documented for this patient, who was diagnosed with HIV 10 weeks ago and started on TDF/3TC/DTG. TDF and 3TC provide dual HBV activity, but knowing HBV co-infection status is important for ongoing monitoring, including liver function tests and abdominal ultrasound as specified in guidelines.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform HBsAg test if not already done, to screen for HBV co-infection per guideline recommendations.
